structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, Palaeozoic and Mesozoic fossil collections are found on continental crust and shelves and are essentially absent from true oceanic islands remote from continents, so present ocean basins were not previously continental land.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using PBDB collections dated Cambrian to Cretaceous (max_ma greater than 66), after excluding continental fragments, accreted terranes and reworked or ex-situ material: at most 2 distinct genuine oceanic-island localities (volcanic or atoll islands on oceanic crust far from continental shelves, e.g. Hawaii, Azores, Galapagos, Ascension, St Helena, Tristan da Cunha) yield in-place Palaeozoic or Mesozoic collections, and these make up under 5% of the Silurian-to-Cretaceous collections located off continental shelves.
structured_output.fail_criterion: More than 5 distinct genuine oceanic-island localities (same exclusions) yield in-place Palaeozoic or Mesozoic collections, or such islands account for 5% or more of the Silurian-to-Cretaceous collections located off continental shelves. A count of 3 to 5 localities is inconclusive.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic island' means volcanic or coral islands on oceanic crust far from continents, not continental fragments such as Madagascar, New Zealand, the Seychelles or New Caledonia. 'Palaeozoic or Secondary formations' maps to PBDB collections with ages from Cambrian to Cretaceous. Only the premise-and-inference Darwin states is tested, which is the absence of old strata on oceanic islands implying long-standing ocean basins. Modern plate tectonics shows that the present ocean floor is younger than about 180 Ma, and that accreted oceanic terranes and ophiolites carry Palaeozoic and Mesozoic material. So the data may show exceptions, which will be reported separately and not counted as genuine oceanic-island localities. A pass confirms only the absence-of-old-strata premise. It does not confirm permanence of the whole ocean and continent configuration, which plate tectonics refutes.

input.prompt: Give the page title, and describe the data available (API, downloads, fields such as paleocoordinates, geological ages, collections).

input.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, Palaeozoic (Silurian-onward) and Mesozoic fossil collections are found on continental crust and continental shelves, and are essentially absent from true oceanic islands remote from continents, so present ocean basins were not previously continental land.
input.pass_criterion: Using PBDB collections with Cambrian-to-Cretaceous ages (and Silurian-to-Cretaceous ages for the continental part), after excluding islands that sit on continental crust or are known accreted terranes: at least 95% of collections lie within continental areas, and fewer than 5% of the remaining oceanic-island occurrences are authentic in-place Palaeozoic or Mesozoic strata. Concretely, the number of such genuine oceanic-island localities (volcanic or atoll islands far from continental shelves, such as Hawaii, Azores, Galapagos, Ascension, St Helena, Tristan da Cunha) must be at most 2.
input.fail_criterion: More than 5 distinct genuine oceanic-island localities (excluding continental fragments, accreted terranes and ex-situ or reworked material) yield in-place Palaeozoic or Mesozoic marine or terrestrial fossil collections, or more than 5% of the non-continental-shelf Silurian-to-Cretaceous collections fall on such islands.
input.interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic island' maps to volcanic or coral islands on oceanic crust far from continents, excluding continental fragments such as Madagascar, New Zealand, the Seychelles and New Caledonia. 'Palaeozoic or Secondary formations' maps to PBDB collections with ages from Cambrian to Cretaceous (Secondary = Mesozoic). 'Oceans and continents in their present areas since the Silurian' is tested only in the weak form Darwin derives, a permanence of ocean basins as inferred from the absence of old strata on oceanic islands. Modern plate tectonics shows ocean floor is younger than about 180 Ma. Accreted oceanic terranes and obducted ophiolites carry Palaeozoic or Mesozoic radiolarian and limestone material, so the data should be expected to show some exceptions; these will be reported separately. A pass is confined to the limited claim of absent old formations on genuine oceanic islands, not to permanence of the whole configuration.
